suggestions.title: Decide the data-rights path before building anything bigger
suggestions.problem: NFL.com Terms section 1.3 allows individual, non-commercial, informational use only and prohibits systematic retrieval or compilation. Almost every planned feature (automated weekly injury pulls, a priced leaderboard, cash rewards) is on the wrong side of that line today.

options.label: Stay strictly personal and non-commercial
options.detail: Keep manual, dated, small-sample reads. Publish only what a person read and attributed. No automation of club or league pages, no redistribution, no rewards.

options.label: Seek written permission or a licence from the league
options.detail: Ask NFL Enterprises / a licensed data partner in writing for the intended use. Until an answer exists, behaviour is unchanged from A.

options.label: Buy a licensed feed that bundles rights
options.detail: A commercial statistics and odds vendor usually grants data rights inside the contract. This is the only path that supports a public product at scale, and it costs money and a contract review.

suggestions.recommendation: A now, B in parallel, C only if the project is meant to be public or commercial. Do not start automating club pages while the answer is outstanding.
suggestions.effort: Low for A, low to start B, high for C
suggestions.impact: Unblocks or forecloses every other suggestion
suggestions.risk: Building first and asking later guarantees rework and possible takedown
suggestions.decision: Open - choose A, B or C

suggestions.title: Get a timestamped market price source (this is the master unlock)
suggestions.problem: Six of the ten gates fail for one reason: there is no price. Without a timestamped price for the exact market and leg, no edge, ROI, closing-line value or ranking can be computed, and the leaderboard stays empty.

options.label: Licensed odds API with archived closing snapshots
options.detail: Highest quality: every leg timestamped, retrievable and contractually usable. Enables G4, G5, G6, G7 and a real leaderboard.

options.label: Manual transcription of one operator's posted prices
options.detail: Small pilot only. The operator's own page is the primary source for its own price, so G1 can pass, but volume is low and the sample gate stays shut for months.

options.label: Keep prices blank
options.detail: Honest, and it means the competition cannot open this season. Suitable only if the project is a teaching exercise.

suggestions.recommendation: B immediately as a pilot with an explicit timestamp on every quote; A if the goal is a real competition this season.
suggestions.impact: Unlocks gates G4, G5, G6, G7 and the leaderboard
suggestions.risk: A single operator's price is not the market; pricing off one book is a known source of false edges
suggestions.decision: Open - choose A, B or C

suggestions.title: Build a timestamped pre-game snapshot archive
suggestions.problem: The only Wednesday practice report is already published, and the Sunday Game Status Report is not due until Friday 4 p.m. New York time. A price built today is stale by rule, so gate G2 fails.

options.label: Two snapshots per week per game
options.detail: Capture the practice report when read and the Game Status Report after its deadline, each with a UTC timestamp and a content hash.

options.label: One snapshot, one hour before kickoff
options.detail: Cheaper, closest to the real decision point, but loses the trail that shows how information moved.

suggestions.recommendation: A, because the delta between the two reports is itself a candidate signal and the archive is what makes G2 passable later.
suggestions.impact: Makes the injury/depth work usable, and makes any future backtest honest
suggestions.risk: Snapshots taken by hand are easy to skip; the process needs a checklist

suggestions.title: Replace 'starter injured' with a measured role weight
suggestions.problem: The current analysis says a first-string player is out and names the next man up. That is a description, not a number, and equal-weighting every position would be an invented assumption.

options.label: Equal weight per first-string absence
options.detail: Simplest and transparent, but treats kicker and quarterback the same and will not survive contact with a backtest.

options.label: Snap-share weight from official participation counts
options.detail: Weight each absence by the share of snaps the player normally takes. Objective and auditable if an official participation source is available.

options.label: Market-implied weight
options.detail: Let the price move caused by the absence define the weight. Circular unless the price is archived before the news, and it needs S-02.

suggestions.recommendation: B, with A kept only as a labelled naive baseline. Do not adopt C before an archive exists.
suggestions.impact: Turns the injury page into a model input instead of a news feed
suggestions.risk: Snap counts are a proxy for importance, not for replacement quality
suggestions.decision: Open - choose A, B or C

suggestions.title: Extend depth coverage from 3 clubs to the whole slate - carefully
suggestions.problem: Depth charts were read for Arizona, Cleveland and San Francisco only, so 25 of the 28 clubs playing this week have no depth evidence. The three-way join (injury status, depth order, prior role) currently works on a third of a slate.

options.label: Manual read of the remaining 25 club charts this week
options.detail: Highest fidelity, roughly one to two hours, and stays inside a personal read of a public page.

options.label: Script the club pages
options.detail: Fast, but conflicts with the no-systematic-retrieval term and would need S-01 settled first.

options.label: Leave the gap and label it
options.detail: Defensible and already published as a flagged gap, but the depth signal stays a pilot.

suggestions.recommendation: A this week, B only after written permission, C only if the week is already gone.
suggestions.impact: Makes the depth-deficiency strategy usable across a full slate
suggestions.risk: Club charts are updated at different times and are not league-normalised
suggestions.decision: Open - choose A, B or C

suggestions.title: Lock the competition rules before anyone competes
suggestions.problem: A leaderboard that ranks strategies without a declared family, a minimum sample and a skill baseline rewards luck and will be gamed by whoever tests the most variants.

options.label: Brier skill score versus the control model, Holm-adjusted, minimum 100 settled bets
options.detail: Published now, before results exist. Losing to the control means the strategy is rejected, not ranked.

options.label: Return-based ranking (ROI)
options.detail: Intuitive but dominated by variance at small samples and trivially improvable by taking long-odds parlays.

options.label: Both, with Brier as the qualifying score and ROI as a displayed diagnostic
options.detail: Combines a stable qualifier with an intuitive number that is explicitly not the ranking.

suggestions.recommendation: C. Never rank on ROI alone at these sample sizes.
suggestions.impact: Prevents the leaderboard from being meaningless
suggestions.risk: Any change to the rules after results arrive invalidates the comparison
suggestions.decision: Open - choose A, B or C

suggestions.title: Build a settled-leg dataset before claiming any parlay correlation
suggestions.problem: The five published correlations are team-season statistics. They do not tell you how a spread leg and a total leg co-move in the same game, which is the only correlation that matters for a same-game parlay.

options.label: Collect settled margin and total pairs for past games
options.detail: One row per game with final score and both leg results. Even 200 games gives usable joint rates and a correlation interval.

options.label: Simulate legs from the rating model
options.detail: Fast and wrong: it measures the model's assumption, not the world's correlation.

options.label: Assume zero correlation
options.detail: The standard parlay error. It systematically misprices correlated legs in both directions.

suggestions.recommendation: A. Leave the leg cells blank until it exists, exactly as they are blank today.
suggestions.impact: Unlocks gate G9 and makes parlay pricing defensible
suggestions.risk: Historical results alone do not give you the price that was available at the time
suggestions.decision: Open - choose A, B or C

suggestions.title: Treat the player-prop pipeline as a separate project
suggestions.problem: Prop combos need official player game logs, a prop price and a settlement rule per market. None of the three exists in this repository.

options.label: Start with one market and one position
options.detail: Quarterback passing yards, using official logs and a single operator's posted line. Small scope, checkable end to end.

options.label: Wait for the licensed feed
options.detail: Correct if props are the goal and a contract is coming. Keeps the repo clean meanwhile.

options.label: Publish a settlement-rule register first
options.detail: No numbers, just the rules that decide whether a leg wins: injury voids, overtime, minimum participation.

suggestions.recommendation: C, then A. Settlement rules decide the outcome more often than the model does, and a void rule can flip a 'win' into a push.
suggestions.impact: Prevents a prop strategy from being scored against the wrong settlement rule
suggestions.risk: Operator rules differ, so a single register must record the operator, not just the market
suggestions.decision: Open - choose A, B or C

suggestions.title: Add a weekly injury-delta engine
suggestions.problem: Wednesday practice participation is not the decision-time state. Between Wednesday and kickoff, designations appear, players are ruled out and backups are named.

options.label: Diff the three weekly reports and publish only the changes
options.detail: Small table, high signal, and it shows whether a player is trending better or worse rather than just 'limited'.

options.label: Keep one snapshot per week
options.detail: Cheap, but it hides the most useful part: the direction of travel.

suggestions.recommendation: A, once S-03 exists. The Friday Game Status Report deadline is published, so the schedule for this is known in advance.
suggestions.impact: Turns injury tracking into a weekly process rather than a page
suggestions.risk: Missed deadlines silently create gaps; the engine must record a miss as a miss

suggestions.title: Adopt a decision log so every choice is reversible
suggestions.problem: Suggestions are being made faster than they are decided. Without a log, a rejected idea comes back next week and an accepted one has no rollback point.

options.label: One page, one row per decision
options.detail: ID, date, decision, owner, rationale, revisit date, rollback. Fits the existing site pattern and costs almost nothing.

options.label: Git commit messages only
options.detail: Free, but hard for a non-technical reader to review.

suggestions.recommendation: A. It is the mechanism that lets you 'choose the best path' rather than accumulate suggestions.
suggestions.risk: A log nobody updates is worse than none; tie each row to a commit

suggestions.title: Separate NFL content from the historical NBA and rental sections
suggestions.problem: The repository now holds three research programmes (NBA, San Francisco rental, NFL) behind one navigation and one generated-build pipeline. Readers cannot tell which era a claim belongs to, and the front page still describes an NBA lab.

options.label: One site, clearly labelled sections with a status banner per section
options.detail: Keep the shared checks and the single build; add an explicit 'archived / active' label to each section.

options.label: Separate repositories
options.detail: Cleanest separation, but duplicates the test harness and loses the shared verification tooling.

options.label: Delete the older sections
options.detail: Not acceptable: it discards reviewed work and its audit trail.

suggestions.recommendation: A. Label first, split later only if the sections start to conflict.
suggestions.impact: Removes the largest source of reader confusion
suggestions.risk: Relabelling can look like a claim change; keep the original pages and add status, do not rewrite history
suggestions.decision: Open - choose A, B or C

suggestions.title: Publish an explicit responsible-gambling block beside every price
suggestions.problem: The site is moving toward prices and a competition, but the support resources and the legal position are not attached to the places where numbers appear.

options.label: One standard block on every page that shows a line
options.detail: Age and jurisdiction limits, the fact that no strategy here is qualified, and a link to support services.

options.label: One page, linked once
options.detail: Lighter, but easy to miss at the point of use.

suggestions.recommendation: A. Prices without that block are the single most likely source of harm in this project.
suggestions.risk: A support line must be official and current; do not invent one

questions.question: What price was actually available for each Week 10 game, at what timestamp, from which operator?
questions.why: Nothing can be called an edge without a price. This single missing input is why the leaderboard is empty.
questions.have: No price. The NFL.com odds path returned 404 on 2026-11-12; no official league price publication was located.
questions.missing: A timestamped quote per market and leg, plus the operator's name and the price type (open, current, close).
questions.discovery: A licensed odds feed, or a manual quote from one operator's own page recorded with a timestamp.

questions.question: Who is first string at each position, and does the source date match the game week?
questions.why: The whole injury and depth analysis depends on knowing whether the unavailable player was actually a starter.
questions.have: Official club depth charts for Arizona, Cleveland and San Francisco; San Francisco's page states 'Updated as of 11/10/26'; the other two print no date.
questions.missing: Depth charts for the other 25 clubs in the slate, and a date on each.
questions.discovery: Each club's own depth-chart page; the league-wide path returned 404.

questions.question: Are Sunday game-status designations available yet, and if not, when will they be?
questions.why: A status of 'out' changes a projection far more than 'limited in practice'. Pricing before designations exist is pricing stale news.
questions.have: Only the Thursday game carries designations (three out, one questionable). The policy deadline for a Sunday Game Status Report is Friday 4 p.m. New York time.
questions.missing: The Friday report itself, plus a record of the exact time it was read.
questions.discovery: The NFL.com injury page after the published deadline, read and timestamped.
questions.status: Answered on timing, not on content

questions.question: What is the injury for a player whose row shows no injury type?
questions.why: A concussion and a hamstring are not the same risk, and several first-string players have no published type on the injury page.
questions.have: The official Wednesday roundup supplies a type for most named players; 21 of 208 rows still have no published type, and those are marked as such rather than guessed.
questions.missing: A type for those 21 rows, and for any player added after Wednesday.
questions.discovery: The next official practice report or the club's own release; otherwise leave blank.

questions.question: Why do four clubs have no Week 10 injury report?
questions.why: Absence from a report could mean a bye, a data gap or a page error. Treating a bye as 'healthy' would be an invention.
questions.have: Chicago, Denver, Philadelphia and Tampa Bay do not appear anywhere in the Week 10 slate. No page consulted labels the reason.
questions.missing: An official statement that these clubs are on bye in Week 10.
questions.discovery: The official 2026 schedule page or the league's weekly release, read directly.

questions.question: What exactly does the injury-report policy require, and by when?
questions.why: It sets the clock for every snapshot and tells you when a missing designation is a violation versus simply not due yet.
questions.have: Quoted policy paragraphs: practice reports on the three days before a game, and a Game Status Report due Wednesday for a Thursday game and Friday for a Sunday game, 4 p.m. New York time.
questions.missing: The full policy document itself. Only the calendar summary has been read.
questions.discovery: The league's operations site or the policy document if it is published; otherwise cite the calendar summary and say so.

questions.question: What use of this data is permitted?
questions.why: It decides whether the project can ever be public, paid or automated.
questions.have: Section 1.3 of the NFL.com Terms: individual, non-commercial, informational use only; systematic retrieval and compilation prohibited without express written consent.
questions.missing: Any written permission, licence or legal opinion specific to this project.
questions.discovery: A written request to the league; a lawyer's read of the terms for the intended use.
questions.status: Answered as a restriction, not as a permission

questions.question: What does 'skill' mean for this competition, and what measurement proves it?
questions.why: Without a fixed definition, any positive run can be presented as skill.
questions.have: A proposal: Brier skill score against the control model, circular block bootstrap interval, Holm adjustment over the declared family of eight, minimum 100 settled bets.
questions.missing: Your sign-off, and the pre-registration commit that freezes it before results.
questions.discovery: Decide now, in S-06; changing it later invalidates the comparison.

questions.question: How many settled observations are needed before a leg correlation is published?
questions.why: A correlation from ten games is noise; publishing it as a number invites trades on it.
questions.have: A proposal: n of at least 100 joint observations and a Fisher interval no wider than 0.2 before any value is displayed.
questions.missing: Your threshold, and the dataset to apply it to.
questions.discovery: Decide with S-07; until then the leg cells stay blank.

questions.question: How is a leg settled when a game goes to overtime, or a player is ruled out after the market opens?
questions.why: Settlement decides the score before the model does. A void is not a win and a push is not a loss.
questions.have: Nothing verified for NFL markets. The repository's separate market-evidence register covers other operators and other sports, and it is explicitly not a universal specification.
questions.missing: The settlement rules of the specific operator whose prices are used.
questions.discovery: Read the operator's own published rules and register them before using its prices.
questions.status: Open - blocking for prop and parlay work

questions.question: Can any reward be offered, and in what form?
questions.why: A reward changes the legal character of the project and can pull in gambling regulation that does not otherwise apply.
questions.have: Merit points only, defined as non-monetary and non-transferable. No cash reward is published.
questions.missing: A legal review of a reward scheme, and the regulator's position in the relevant jurisdiction.
questions.discovery: Legal advice; the applicable gaming regulator's published guidance.

questions.question: Who refreshes the data each week, at what time, and what happens when they miss?
questions.why: Every gate assumes a timestamp. A missed week must be recorded as missing, not quietly backfilled.
questions.have: A single ad-hoc capture on 2026-11-12 with no roster of owners.
questions.missing: An owner, a deadline, and a rule for a missed snapshot.
questions.discovery: S-03 and S-09 define the process; publishing it is the answer.

questions.question: How should a club with 'No Injuries Reported' be treated?
questions.why: It is not the same as a fully healthy roster; it means the page records nothing.
questions.have: Two clubs (Baltimore, Los Angeles Chargers) show exactly that text, and are carried as a row that says so rather than as zero injuries.
questions.missing: A decision on whether that is an input of zero or an unknown in the model.
questions.discovery: Decide in S-04; the safe default is unknown.

questions.question: What happens to a strategy when its triggering condition disappears - for example a quarterback returns?
questions.why: Strategies keyed to a backup starting silently die when the starter returns, and a dead strategy can keep 'winning' on stale logic.
questions.have: Nothing. The strategy register has no lifecycle field.
questions.missing: An expiry rule per strategy, and a review date.
questions.discovery: Add expiry and review columns in S-10 and revise the strategy register.

questions.question: How is a team-level correlation kept from being read as a bet-leg correlation?
questions.why: The published correlations are between season aggregates across teams. Using them to price a two-leg parlay would be a category error.
questions.have: Explicit labels on the correlation page and in the data file; the leg-level cells are blank.
questions.missing: Nothing factual. The open question is whether any reader or future contributor will ignore the label.
questions.discovery: Keep the warning adjacent to the table, not only in documentation.

flags.item: No market price anywhere on this site
flags.detail: Every market-line, edge, ROI and closing-line-value cell is blank. The NFL.com odds path returned 404 on 2026-11-12 and no official league price source was located. Blank is the verified state, not an oversight.

flags.item: Sunday game-status designations do not exist yet
flags.detail: Only the Thursday game carries designations. The policy deadline for the Sunday Game Status Report is Friday 4 p.m. New York time, so the absence is expected rather than missing data.

flags.item: Injury type is not published for 21 of 208 rows
flags.detail: Those rows show a practice status but no injury description on either official page read. They are published with a blank injury cell and a note, never with a guessed type.

flags.item: Depth coverage is 3 of the 28 clubs in the slate
flags.detail: Arizona, Cleveland and San Francisco were read. The other 25 clubs have no depth evidence, so any league-wide depth claim would be unsupported.

flags.item: Depth charts are club publications and only one prints a date
flags.detail: San Francisco prints 'Updated as of 11/10/26'. Arizona and Cleveland print no date, so their ordering cannot be tied to a time of day.

flags.item: Four clubs are absent from the Week 10 slate for an unexplained reason
flags.detail: Chicago, Denver, Philadelphia and Tampa Bay appear in the standings but not in any Week 10 game or injury section. No page consulted states why, so no bye is asserted.

flags.item: The league publishes no depth-chart endpoint at the checked paths
flags.detail: Two league depth-chart paths returned 404 on 2026-11-12. This documents the paths checked, not the absence of every league depth publication.

flags.item: Model parameters are design choices, not official facts
flags.detail: Shrinkage of 4 pseudo-games, a 2.0-point home-field term, a 13.0-point logistic scale and a 2.37 Pythagorean exponent are all project choices. Every projection is therefore published with a range across a parameter grid.
Five correlations across 32 team rows are published. They are not leg correlations and cannot price a parlay. The leg-level cells are blank and flagged.

flags.item: Two source typos are transcribed and preserved
flags.detail: The official roundup writes 'limted' (Miami, Darrell Baker Jr.) and 'hamtring' (Carolina, Jaelan Phillips). Status is normalised to the page's own categories and the typical spelling is noted, without silently editing the source.

flags.item: Standings columns beyond the ones used are unlabelled in the extracted page
flags.detail: Only W, L, T, PCT, PF, PA and NET PTS are used, and those seven are confirmed by the page legend and by two arithmetic identities on all 32 rows. The remaining columns are ignored rather than guessed at.

flags.item: Cash rewards and any gambling-linked use are not cleared
flags.detail: NFL.com Terms section 1.3 permits individual non-commercial informational use only. No licence and no legal review of a reward scheme exists, so the competition pays nothing.

flags.item: A player on injured reserve disappears from the weekly injury page
flags.detail: Malik Willis does not appear on the Week 10 injury page because he was placed on injured reserve. The transaction is only visible in a separate article, so a page-only reader would miss that Miami's starter is unavailable.
flags.status: Detected - covered by a separate source

flags.item: Legacy sections of this repository still carry pre-NFL claims
flags.detail: The front page, README and package name still describe an NBA research lab, and older 'verified' directories exist as redirects. Nothing was deleted; the NFL section is additive and this flag records the inconsistency for manual review.

qa.question: Did this session originate any actual NFL line?
qa.answer: It produced model-implied spreads and totals for all 14 Week 10 games from official standings, each with a sensitivity range. It did not produce a market line, because no verified price exists and inventing one would be fabrication.

qa.question: How many strategies passed validation?
qa.answer: None. Eight strategies are registered and all are blocked, most of them on the price gate. The leaderboard is empty on purpose.

qa.question: What is the strongest single finding?
qa.answer: Depth, not injury, is the missing variable. Five first-string players in this slate have no replacement listed at all on their club's depth chart, so 'next man up' cannot be evaluated for them at any price.

qa.question: Which injury information is verified twice?
qa.answer: Practice status is read from the NFL.com injury page and again from the official Wednesday roundup. Every player named in both was compared; the two pages agree on every matched player.

qa.question: Is a team-level correlation useful for parlays?
qa.answer: No. It describes how teams relate to each other across a season. A parlay needs the joint behaviour of two legs in the same game, which is not computed here and is published as blank.

qa.question: Can luck be removed from the results?
qa.answer: No. It can be bounded and reported, which is what the bootstrap and Holm gates do, but with 14 upcoming games there is nothing to bound yet. Any ranking at this sample size would be luck dressed as skill.

qa.question: What would unblock the most work fastest?
qa.answer: A timestamped price source (S-02). It is the single input that fails the most gates, and everything else in the protocol is already specified and implemented.

qa.question: What is the biggest legal risk?
qa.answer: Treating league data as free to compile and publish. Section 1.3 of the NFL.com Terms permits individual non-commercial informational use and prohibits systematic retrieval and compilation without written consent.

qa.question: How much of the Week 10 injury picture is known today?
qa.answer: Practice participation for 208 player rows across 28 clubs, with seven players already ruled out and one questionable. Sunday designations are due Friday and do not exist yet.

qa.question: Are the model's numbers reproducible by someone else?
qa.answer: Yes. The inputs are a 32-row CSV with a source per row, the parameters are in the repository, and the build is deterministic and hash-checked in CI.

qa.question: What was verified for this session versus inherited?
qa.answer: Every NFL value here was read on 2026-11-12. Nothing NFL-related was inherited, because no NFL content existed in the repository before this session. Inherited NBA and rental content is out of scope and unchanged.

qa.question: What should be decided first?
qa.answer: S-01 (data rights) and S-02 (price source). Every other suggestion either depends on them or can proceed regardless; these two decide whether the project can be more than a private exercise.
